title: Print an owner line
prompt: owner is a supplied string and count is a supplied whole number. Print one line with the owner, a colon and a space, then the count, as in Ana: 2. When owner is the empty string, print Unassigned in its place. When count is 0, print the word none in its place. Both rules can apply to the same line: Unassigned: none.
hints: The two rules are independent. Does your code handle each one whatever the other does?
Work out the name part and the count part separately, each with its own if, then print them together.
Use one string variable for the name and one for the count text. Change each only when its own rule applies.
checkLabels: The line must show the owner or Unassigned, a colon and a space, then the count or none.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Treats the two rules as one: an empty owner always prints none.
Handles the empty owner but not the zero count.

feedback: Find the failing case and check each half of the line on its own. The owner rule and the count rule do not depend on each other.
